passage:
A small shop placed a handwritten sign in its window: "We are short of staff today. Service may be slow. Thank you for your patience."
Customers were more understanding than usual. Some waited quietly. One even helped carry used cups to the counter.
The owner later said the sign changed the mood of the shop. Without it, slow service looked like carelessness. With it, customers saw a human problem.
The sign did not make the line shorter, but it made waiting easier.
Clear communication can reduce anger. People often react not only to delay, but to not knowing why delay is happening.
